name: Tatiana Lysenko
milestone_by_age_26: Won all-around gold at the 1990 World Cup Final in Brussels at age 15, followed by two Olympic gold medals at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at age 17.
early_history_summary: Started gymnastics at age 7 in Kherson under coach Oleg Ostapenko at Dynamo Kherson, part of the dominant Soviet gymnastics pipeline. Made her senior debut in 1990 and immediately won the World Cup all-around, upsetting 1989 World Champion Svetlana Boginskaya.
family_context_summary: Born to an engineer father and physician mother in Kherson, Ukrainian SSR, providing a middle-class professional household.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet gymnastics pipeline, elite coaching, early specialization, physical talent
evidence_summary: Born to professional parents in Kherson, Lysenko began gymnastics at age 7 under coach Oleg Ostapenko at Dynamo Kherson, part of the dominant Soviet gymnastics system. She won the World Cup all-around at 15 and Olympic gold at 17, benefiting from elite coaching and the Soviet gymnastics pipeline. Her rapid rise reflects both physical talent and the concentrated training environment of the Soviet sports system.
starting_point: Born in Kherson, Ukrainian SSR to an engineer father and physician mother; entered the Soviet gymnastics pipeline at age 7.
current_position: Lives in the United States; graduated from University of San Francisco Law School, passed the California Bar in 2005, and works in PR/IR liaison.

name: José Aldo
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WEC featherweight championship by defeating Mike Brown via TKO at WEC 44 on November 18, 2009 at age 23, becoming one of the youngest champions in MMA; awarded first UFC featherweight championship belt in November 2010 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Growing up poor in Manaus, Brazil, Aldo started capoeira at 14 before switching to jiu-jitsu. At 17, he moved alone to Rio de Janeiro to train at Nova União under André Pederneiras, sleeping on gym mats and eating one meal per day. He made his professional MMA debut at 17 in August 2004 and compiled a 16-1 record before winning the WEC title.
family_context_summary: Born to a bricklayer father and housewife mother in Manaus, Brazil; grew up in humble circumstances with limited financial resources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty-driven urgency, early fighting immersion, dedicated coach, Brazilian MMA ecosystem
evidence_summary: Born into poverty in Manaus with a bricklayer father, Aldo started capoeira at 14 before switching to jiu-jitsu. At 17, he moved alone to Rio de Janeiro to train at Nova União under André Pederneiras, sleeping on gym mats and eating one meal per day. His pro MMA debut at 17 and rapid rise to WEC champion by 23 reflect both physical talent and extreme dedication driven by economic necessity. The Brazilian MMA/BJJ ecosystem provided the training infrastructure for his development.
starting_point: Born in Manaus, Brazil to a bricklayer father and housewife mother; grew up in humble circumstances in a poor neighborhood.
current_position: Retired from MMA and inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame in 2023; widely regarded as the greatest featherweight in MMA history with a 18-fight win streak and 7 UFC title defenses.

name: Johnny Logan
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Eurovision Song Contest on April 19, 1980 at age 25 with 'What's Another Year,' which topped the charts in eight countries and launched his international career.
early_history_summary: Son of Irish tenor Patrick O'Hagan, Logan grew up in a musical household in Howth, Co. Dublin. He learned guitar by 13, began writing songs, and toured with his father as a teenager. He apprenticed as an electrician while performing in pubs and cabaret acts, releasing his first single in 1978 before winning Eurovision in 1980.
